---|---|---
|
# Drop Site News is Under Attack From an Authoritarian Government
### We're right where we wanna be
| | | [Ryan Grim](https://substack.com/@ryangrim)
---
| Sep 11
---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f51171b0-3476-4565-8bdd-50c0c84a8dac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Barely two months into Drop Site's tenure, we have made enemies of at least three governments, been banned in one country, and censored by the largest social-media platform in the world.
Pakistan's military government has banned Drop Site News from being read inside the country, following a sweeping series of investigative reports that have rocked the embattled leadership. The military followed the ban with threats of further legal action and accusations from military-linked officials that Drop Site is "being funded by Jew and Indian lobbies," mixing antisemitism with anti-Indian attitudes. Instagram and Facebook, meanwhile, have periodically blocked the sharing of Drop Site's coverage of the ongoing genocide in Gaza on Meta platforms. And following an investigation into the U.S.-linked attorney general of Ecuador, allies of the right-wing government have accused Drop Site of being established and funded by the leftist party of Rafael Correa for the express purpose of undermining the government. We're just getting started, but drawing these kinds of unhinged and ferocious responses from centers of power was precisely our goal when we launched Drop Site News. There will be plenty more to come -- especially as we can now rely on our growing base of readers to fight back.
Drop Site is the new independent, non-profit news organization I founded with Jeremy Scahill, Nausicaa Renner, and other former colleagues. **If you 're not getting our updates and you want to be signed up,[ please do that here](https://substack.com/redirect/60ff7529-cb56-41c0-becb-5be0edc85666?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Our journalism is free but relies on paid subscribers or[ one-time donors ](https://substack.com/redirect/0868df85-0d54-4cf8-9e3d-d93741fb2015?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)to power it. ([Contributions are tax-deductible](https://substack.com/redirect/0868df85-0d54-4cf8-9e3d-d93741fb2015?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the fullest extent of the law.)
It is in Pakistan where the pushback has been the most intense, as the state's descent into authoritarianism has accelerated. [In July, Drop Site News](https://substack.com/redirect/b5e25d55-f00c-4972-95cd-d4cb7dc3aac0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) exposed the existence of a secret operation run by the Pakistani Army, called the Army Agahi Network (AAN). The program deploys thousands of military officers, operating under aliases and fake accounts, to act as trolls in online combat. By design, the program requires them to violate their constitutional oath to remain apolitical.
The primary source of the report was an individual in the Pakistani security establishment outraged by the military's design to launch the program. The leak itself also highlighted growing discontent within the armed forces against its leadership. The response from the Pakistani government to the story was fast, furious, and chaotic.
In August, Drop Site [published audio](https://substack.com/redirect/1f7f2144-4904-4d51-98af-cb4ae4fac29a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of an extortion attempt by a Pakistan government official. After a half dozen men abducted a Pakistani man, the government official called the man's brother, a citizen of Australia, with an offer: Stop criticizing the government publicly, and his brother would be returned. When he initially refused, they began torturing his brother, producing screams audible on the recording. The resulting video went viral in Pakistan and in the United States, and that evening the internet slowed to a crawl in Pakistan.
Not content to ban one foreign news outlet, the Pakistani government has now moved to control the entire internet. Pakistan's Ministry of Information Technology had previously [allocated a staggering $135 million](https://substack.com/redirect/4e6fa91c-e463-4eaa-b436-61832f08904d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a massive investment--to procure a national firewall and web traffic monitoring tool, [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/96967465-2724-49cd-9426-bdf7bbbe8afc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the support of China.
Shortly after Drop Site exposed the AAN program, the government hastily tested the firewall. The decision has caused widespread internet disruptions that have quite literally, [breaking the Pakistani internet](https://substack.com/redirect/792654ae-2750-4121-b2e9-f85e57623317?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by slowing download and upload speeds to a crawl across service providers. Users widely reported being unable to share media on platforms such as WhatsApp, which are vital to commerce and daily life.
The economic repercussions of these disruptions are already being felt, with some estimates stating that the Pakistani economy stands to [lose up to $300 million yearly](https://substack.com/redirect/6638c1da-e561-4da3-9647-84ba9dd6548d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a result of the firewall. Freelancers on platforms like Fiverr have seen their [accounts suspended](https://substack.com/redirect/ff9bab45-8ac7-42aa-a772-3202a5666792?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) due to "internet disruptions," while the IT sector as a whole, a small bright spot in Pakistan's otherwise struggling economy, faces a real threat that the new online [censorship regime and firewall](https://substack.com/redirect/fb55a657-f809-407a-9583-ce77077d610a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) will stifle its hopes for growth.
In a press conference on August 5, the director general of the ISPR also made a [legal threat](https://substack.com/redirect/70a197e5-6df8-469a-95d2-6ab30c3484cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against foreign news outlets covering Pakistan. "Whoever -- whether in Pakistan or abroad and irrespective of their position -- is found spreading propaganda against the Pakistan Army, creating a distance between the army and the people, or is found to be involved in spreading fake news, the army will take necessary legal action against it, and there is a whole process for it," he said.
This August the government also abducted Raoof Hasan, the chief spokesperson for the party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan. While in custody, Hasan's phone was searched, where messages from a Drop Site reporter were found. Though the messages were no more than a typical exchange between a journalist and a spokesperson, the government shared them with Pakistani media, which spent days broadcasting [claims](https://substack.com/redirect/e9dc5426-453a-4dda-92d2-f1060ec5aa2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the texts revealed "anti-Pakistan propaganda."
The government of Ecuador and its allies seem similarly unprepared for scrutiny at the hands of investigative reporters. Last week, [Drop Site, in partnership with The Intercept Brasil, published an investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/1d6d68ad-8b18-4fab-86ed-56c778d5290c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) into the state's attorney general, Diana Salazar, based on a cache of text messages she sent to an Ecuadorian judge and to a former member of parliament-turned-fugitive. The story, published in English, Spanish, and Portuguese, revealed how Salazar is using her office to pursue cases with political motives, including attacks on the left-wing political party -- all in alliance with the U.S. government.
The messages we reviewed also included highly sensitive information about investigations and cases pursued by the attorney general's Office and the U.S. government. The story exploded in Ecuador, being widely read and shared and sending shockwaves through the country and around South America. The messages had been a source of intrigue in Ecuador, and Drop Site's investigation was the first major international report regarding the chats and the allegations of misconduct
The story's readership also came with a wide array of wild rumors and attacks. The traditional Ecuadorian press has attempted to throw cold water on the story: pundits and supporters Salazar have published op-eds and analyses accusing Drop Site of being a Chavista or Correista outlet. Fake images began circulating, saying that Drop Site was created by Correa supporters, with the sole goal of attacking Salazar, and lambasting us as "narco-journalists." Highly-edited and dramatic videos also circulated online, saying our reporting was part of a coordinated attack from Correa's political party, and that Correistas "financed two unknown journalists, Jose Olivares and Ryan Grim" to publish the story.
If you can help us fight back, [please consider making a tax-deductible contribution](https://substack.com/redirect/0868df85-0d54-4cf8-9e3d-d93741fb2015?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). For [more on ways to give,](https://substack.com/redirect/2779a119-8275-4bab-9af1-cb5798f35b3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) see our FAQ here.

Vivek Ramaswamy

Today, there's only one thing to talk about - **September 11, 2001 and remembering the worst American tragedy in our country 's history**.

September 11th was the worst terror attack on this country, claiming more lives in one day. It demonstrated unbelievable heroism by our first responders, running into buildings to save lives and many perished.

On September 11, 2001, I was on my way to New York City to go to work. I was just arriving at Grand Central when we heard the news. As a physician, I went to my local hospital to see if I could help. I spoke with hospital coordinators, emergency coordinators at the time and their best suggestion was we're all set and to get out of New York City.
_It was hours before I could reach my wife and my kids and tell them that I was OK and many of us had those feelings about our loved ones. Where were they? were they ok._ There was no transportation and I started walking north like so many others. I made my way up to Harlem and the Metro North started running again.
Thanks for reading Michael's Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

In the days following September 11th, I've never seen this country more united. This was not about race, religion, political, sexual orientation. It was about all Americans being united.
**September 12th was one of the most unifying days in our country 's history. All Americans united for one common cause to build ourselves up and launch a war on terror. For years we say on September 11th we were divided; on September 12 we were united.
**
It is unity that has been missing in our country for many years as Americans. We need to put our differences aside. We need to unite and fight our enemies domestic and abroad. We need to be united here in the US and have conversations with those we think we may disagree with as I have found we always have a lot more in common when we come together and talk with each other.

Today on September 11th as we remember 23 years have gone by and terror still exists everywhere. We are subject to terror attack in the United States and our allies are subject to terror attacks throughout the world.

I pray that we never have another September 11th in this country.

For all of us, Never Forget September 11th and in the current climate - Never Again is Now. It is critical to support our first responders and allowing them to do the jobs that they are meant to do and were born to do. They run into a fire while most run from it.

**Today is not a political day. Today is a day of remembrance and tomorrow on September 12th, let 's all strive to be united once again and carry on the mission started on September 12, 2001. We can do that by**
* Finding the the common ground between us; and
* Healing this divisiveness that persists for no reason.

I'm a physician and I spent my entire career and continue to spend my career healing my patients, listen to my patients and treating them.

Let's make this anniversary the most united one we can as a country and continue the healing process.
Sharing is Caring - so if you like the message please pass it on.

The presidential debate took place on Tuesday. How did it go and what will the impact be?
Kamala Harris had the more important assignment. Her job was to seem commanding, confident, and competent in the face of Trump for 90 minutes. 29% of Americans prior to the debate said that they still didn’t have enough information about her to have an opinion. Kamala’s goal was to make it natural for millions of Americans to imagine her as commander-in-chief.
Kamala cleared the bar. And in that respect, Tuesday was a huge victory for her. She was sharp, composed and on message throughout. She got an enormous number of digs in and seemed completely unintimidated by Trump, even bemused.
Trump on the other hand wanted to come across as in control and non-contemptuous while tying Kamala Harris to a very unpopular Joe Biden. His message definitely meandered. He went down numerous blind alleys. He got more airtime but it didn’t necessarily help him.
Kamala was thoroughly prepared and it showed. Her performance reassured many. 63% of viewers in one poll deemed her the victor, not too far off from Trump’s margin over Joe Biden in the last debate in June. I think Kamala’s performance will win over a sliver of wavering swing voters in the swing states who wanted to make sure she was up to the challenge before committing to vote for her. Taylor Swift’s endorsement may be a sign for those waiting for this kind of performance.
What impact will it have on the race? It probably keeps it neck-and-neck. The polling had started to shift to Trump in the days leading up to the debate. Trump’s following is locked in and the debate will have no impact on his voters. His ‘the country is going to hell’ message works for his audience. Remember, about 75% of Americans think we’re on the wrong track. This race is going to come down to a relative handful of voters in the swing districts.
The single biggest thing that Kamala could do to drive her momentum is to start doing interviews, not just with major national press but with local outlets in the swing states and unconventional shows with major reach (e.g. “Hot Ones” with Harris would do a ton of views). Given that she now has answers to most every major topic memorized and prepared, they should get her out there. The most important asset every campaign has is candidate time, and doing press is one of the highest-leverage ways to utilize that time.
There may not even be another presidential debate. The time for risk aversion has passed. Now is the time to try and win by putting your top player on the field as much as possible. Don’t play not to lose. Play to win.
Will Kamala Harris be the next President? The odds went up after Tuesday night. She did the most important thing – she was presidential. Less than 8 weeks to go.

Peter, Last night, Vice President Kamala Harris took the debate stage and sent a clear message to the American people about what’s at stake in this election. Harris contrasted Trump’s lies, misinformation, and negativity with real facts, policy and patriotism. She laid out her plans to build upon the Biden Administration’s historic progress, like lowering costs for Americans and codifying the protections of _Roe v. Wade_ into law. But there’s one thing above all else that really stands out from last night’s debate: **In order to implement any policies that will move our nation forward, we must protect our democracy.** If elected, self-declared wanna-be dictator Donald Trump and his Project 2025 would eviscerate the fundamental democratic values that have made this the greatest country on earth: the rule of law, separation of powers, checks and balances, and global stability. That’s why so many conservative Republicans and former Trump officials continue to support Harris over Trump — because they know Trump is simply not fit to be president. **It’s time for our nation to turn the page on Trump's grievance-filled fear, division, and hate. And last night, Kamala Harris showed us the promise of a brighter, better future for all Americans.** We're not going back, Peter. But we have our work cut out for us between now and November 5th. We must get voters out to the polls to elect Kamala Harris and keep Donald Trump out of the White House. clean_body: | Peter, Last night, Vice President Kamala Harris took the debate stage and sent a clear message to the American people about what’s at stake in this election. Harris contrasted Trump’s lies, misinformation, and negativity with real facts, policy and patriotism. She laid out her plans to build upon the Biden Administration’s historic progress, like lowering costs for Americans and codifying the protections of Roe v. Wade into law. But there’s one thing above all else that really stands out from last night’s debate: In order to implement any policies that will move our nation forward, we must protect our democracy. If elected, self-declared wanna-be dictator Donald Trump and his Project 2025 would eviscerate the fundamental democratic values that have made this the greatest country on earth: the rule of law, separation of powers, checks and balances, and global stability. That’s why so many conservative Republicans and former Trump officials continue to support Harris over Trump — because they know Trump is simply not fit to be president. It’s time for our nation to turn the page on Trump's grievance-filled fear, division, and hate. And last night, Kamala Harris showed us the promise of a brighter, better future for all Americans. We're not going back, Peter. But we have our work cut out for us between now and November 5th. We must get voters out to the polls to elect Kamala Harris and keep Donald Trump out of the White House. We have to spread Democrats’ message and support candidates up and down the ballot who will bolster the Harris Administration’s strides toward progress. | Friend, I’m Riley Gaines. You may have heard my name in the news. I’m an All-American swimmer -- but I’m better known for my role in the fight to save women’s sports.
Women and girls have a right to compete fairly, and to private locker rooms. I speak out strongly for all female athletes like me who’ve been forced to compete against men. **Just this year, a female golfer lost her spot in the U.S. Women’s Open qualifier at Bradenton to a man, James “Hailey” Davidson.** Then, USA Today _took down_ a brilliant op-ed by Republican Senator John Kennedy. name: Callie Barr
subject: Remembering 9/11
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Callie Barr for Congress
body:
Today, as we remember the lives lost and honor that day’s heroes, I ask that we renew our commitment to building a better future–a future where our nation’s leaders prioritize the well-being of people, not partisan politics.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92614738/497712229/1201310784?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDUwMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWJkMDcxNDUtNWY3MC1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkYThhYWU5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hhLgF5eX7KIVpMwy5rFWSee9beCEWGGy5mewaNTxHvk=&emci=a7be760e-4b70-ef11-991a-6045bda8aae9&emdi=9bd07145-5f70-ef11-991a-6045bda8aae9&ceid=9697413)
---
| Peter,

On this day 23 years ago, our nation faced unimaginable loss and tragedy. Like many Americans, I remember where I was when I first heard the news of the attacks on September 11, 2001. That day, we witnessed immense courage, sacrifice, and the undeniable strength of our country coming together. First responders, service members, and ordinary citizens put everything on the line to protect their fellow Americans.

For me, 9/11 became a pivotal moment in my life. Matt’s first call was to a military recruiter’s office to enlist. Just two days after his high school graduation, he left for Marine Corps boot camp and soon deployed to Iraq. That marked the start of my long journey as a veterans’ advocate.

After my husband Matt’s service left him with an undiagnosed brain injury and post-traumatic stress, I saw firsthand how our system sometimes falls short in supporting those who give so much for us.

We honor our country and those sacrifices by moving forward together. And we make sure our veterans, military families, and communities get the care and support they deserve.

Today, as we remember the lives lost and honor that day’s heroes, I ask that we renew our commitment to building a better future–a future where our nation’s leaders prioritize the well-being of people, not partisan politics.

With gratitude,

Callie

On 9/11/01, I was a 19-year-old college sophomore. I am among the last generations who was an adult prior to 9/11, and observed the changes our world and country went through since. With that context, I need to make three important points today.
**Let 's Address This.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bc3a2bb5-69ee-4d50-bae2-c262b2f300b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The annual Tribute in Light illuminates lower Manhattan in honor of 9/11. Credit: Gary Hershorn/ABC News
**Let's Address This with Qasim Rashid is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..crU1YgkswG-Lj_oGNQYUCp7LhVtlgVFmz_z2g9QZW2A?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=148726264)
## Lesson 1: Perspective in mourning
On 9/11 we mourn 2977 fellow Americans. Innocent people viciously ripped away from us by terrorists and extremists. We pray for the 2977 departed, we remember them, and we cherish their memories. And too often the conversation stops there. But there is so much more we must remember.
In the 23 years since we lost roughly 10,000 American soldiers. Depending on various estimates, hundreds of thousands of Afghan and Iraq civilians were killed in the two subsequent wars after 9/11. Our government wasted more than $8 Trillion on the "war on terror"--a shocking $250 million a day for more than two decades. And we are no safer or closer to peace or justice today, than we were back then.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1dabf83a-2ef5-4dcb-9f0a-57ba3bf41834?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In the days and weeks after 9/11, Rep Barbara Lee stood with moral courage to oppose the war, and she was right. History has tragically proven her more right than I believe even she might have imagined. After 23 long, painful years, my prayer is that our future policies are not built on invasion and war, but on justice and diplomacy, on accountability and transparency. On our Constitutional promise of due process and human rights.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..crU1YgkswG-Lj_oGNQYUCp7LhVtlgVFmz_z2g9QZW2A?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=148726264)
## Lesson 2: Perspective in history
Uninformed memes like the one below have begun popping up over the last few years, dangerously whitewashing post 9/11 America by falsely calling us a "unified" country on 9/12.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6c74d2b3-ffe6-4e5f-b242-b0280f51ec9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
If even after 23 years you think the weeks or months after 9/11 were days of unity, you have not been paying attention to the BIPOC people and Muslims in America. The people in your life who feared for our safety and suffered a massive spike in hate crimes for something we had nothing to do with.
Yes, the myth of "unity" means [ignoring the massive spike in anti-Muslim, anti-Hindu, anti-Sikh, and anti-Arab hate crimes post 9/11](https://substack.com/redirect/26b57b45-cd77-48e4-9d7d-a6361ec2f5f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It means ignoring the Patriot Act (which even some Democrats in Congress still recklessly vote for), the [NYPD's illegal warrantless spying on American citizens who are Muslim](https://substack.com/redirect/b198c036-d4d1-4d62-8588-36b69ad00396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the [dozens of states who tried to pass "anti-Shariah" bills](https://substack.com/redirect/57551176-6f4c-41b5-90bb-6b603764a0b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Guantanamo Bay, CIA torture, indiscriminate drone strikes, & the Muslim Ban--all which denied the justice our Constitution promises.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a715f6ec-1d06-4f7c-a2ec-7e541893155b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A reminder that Trump's racist Muslim Ban had nothing to do with 9/11 or national security, and everything to do with bigotry and racism.
These are all connected.
The "unity" was if you unquestionably supported what George W. Bush called "a crusade," that "God told him" to wage. Otherwise, you were unpatriotic. "You're either with us, or you're with the terrorists," Bush famously said--whitewashing objections to killing of hundreds of thousands of Afghan and Iraqi civilians
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/014088c2-7c85-4047-95a3-39eef3823927?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Instead, the unity we actually need is unity built on justice, as our Constitution requires. On ensuring we do not scapegoat innocent people, but always uphold due process for all people--especially when it's hard.
If we can't uphold justice when it's hard, it was never justice we upheld.

## Lesson 3: Perspective on the future
Revisionist history of "unity" undermines the lived experiences of BIPOC people and Muslims. Let's instead reflect on our past errors, and ensure a future nation built on justice. The reality is that anti-Muslim hate crimes are still at record highs. Donald Trump [has promised an even more aggressive anti-Muslim ban if he's reelected](https://substack.com/redirect/0f2c4347-5a70-4c9a-b591-afe7933853ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And it is unsurprising that Trump promises more Islamophobic bigotry, given that Islamophobia remains an acceptable form of bigotry in American politics today.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f6468e66-033d-4063-8571-0531074a7026?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Florida Republican Randy Fine uses hashtag "Muslim terror" in a pathetic attempt to mock Muslims for not eating pork
And [as I've written recently](https://substack.com/@qasimrashid/p-148477597), even the Department of Justice tragically demonstrates a double standard in how they respond to the murder and kidnapping of American citizens--condemning and prosecuting crimes committed by Hamas, but ignoring those crimes against American citizens committed by Netanyahu.
The future also requires we do right by those who continue to suffer from 9/11 in the United States. How many people realize that [more FDNY members have died from World Trade Center illnesses than killed on 9/11](https://substack.com/redirect/47ca0cb0-ec36-47c3-a372-bd953967cb80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)? Our nation's lack of guaranteed universal healthcare as a human right is a perpetual atrocity inflicted upon our populace.
If we want to ensure we learn from the lessons of history, our future must be grounded in absolute justice. That means rejecting double standards in legal accountability, rejecting discriminatory legislation against marginalized communities, and rejecting anti-Muslim bigotry and Islamophobia. Today we mourn those lost over the last 23 years. The people lost, the opportunities lost, and the rights lost. And the best way to honor what we lost, is to ensure we truly uphold justice for the next 23 years, and beyond, to demand true justice for all. True love of humanity requires it. Just remember, love isn't a word, it's meaningful action for justice. And that is something we must Never Forget

name: Tamie Wilson
subject: Reflecting on 9/11: A day that changed us forever
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP33/1/100067/images/LOGO.jpg]
Friends,
Twenty-three years ago, I was a single woman living in Boston, excited about the future and my new life in the big city.
I felt safe, almost invincible – like I had all the time in the world. But that all changed the day the towers fell, and we learned about the attacks on the Pentagon and United Flight 93.
I’ll never forget watching the news with my neighbors, seeing the first plane hit and then, in real-time, the second.
We sat in stunned silence, eventually breaking down into tears as we realized what was happening.
The men responsible had taken off from Logan Airport just down the street from us, and the entire city felt frozen in fear.
For the first time, I realized the U.S. wasn’t immune to the chaos of the world.
Back then, we watched the Bush administration and the GOP falter, sending our troops into dangerous, misguided wars that left us less secure.
Those same sensibilities have only worsened with the ULTRA-MAGA takeover of the Republican Party, where reckless decisions and extremism now define their approach to most issues, including national security. But now I see radicals in my own country attacking our Capitol and our elected officials’ loved ones. I never thought I’d see those days here, in the U.S..
Now, as I run for Congress, I often reflect on 9/11 and the profound impact it had on our geopolitics, shaping my views on safety and security in lasting ways.
The threats we face today are different but no less serious.
That’s why I’m asking for your support today – to help build a campaign prioritizing real safety measures for American families, one that rejects the extremism of Jim Jordan and ULTRA-MAGA and treats domestic terrorism for the serious threat it is . [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240911_9_11_anni_link1]
Jordan and his cronies refuse to denounce those who spread conspiracy theories and sow division, creating a dangerous environment for all of us. You would think after Trump got shot they would tone it down, but oh no! To top it off, they’re already sowing doubt in the election.
After 9/11, we were told that the biggest threat came from abroad. Today, the FBI says domestic terrorism is our greatest concern, and yet, we’ve barely scratched the surface of addressing it.
Especially when Jim Jordan defends and aids insurrectionists, it's clear that we need new leadership that values bipartisan politics, common-sense policies, collaboration with allies, and a proactive approach to keeping us safe.
I believe in pushing for meaningful solutions—like targeting domestic terrorism prevention, funding de-radicalization programs, and supporting mental health resources to stop violence before it starts.

clean_body: [] Friends, Twenty-three years ago, I was a single woman living in Boston, excited about the future and my new life in the big city. I felt safe, almost invincible – like I had all the time in the world. But that all changed the day the towers fell, and we learned about the attacks on the Pentagon and United Flight 93. I’ll never forget watching the news with my neighbors, seeing the first plane hit and then, in real-time, the second. We sat in stunned silence, eventually breaking down into tears as we realized what was happening. The men responsible had taken off from Logan Airport just down the street from us, and the entire city felt frozen in fear. For the first time, I realized the U.S. wasn’t immune to the chaos of the world. Back then, we watched the Bush administration and the GOP falter, sending our troops into dangerous, misguided wars that left us less secure. Those same sensibilities have only worsened with the ULTRA-MAGA takeover of the Republican Party, where reckless decisions and extremism now define their approach to most issues, including national security. But now I see radicals in my own country attacking our Capitol and our elected officials’ loved ones. I never thought I’d see those days here, in the U.S.. Now, as I run for Congress, I often reflect on 9/11 and the profound impact it had on our geopolitics, shaping my views on safety and security in lasting ways. The threats we face today are different but no less serious. That’s why I’m asking for your support today – to help build a campaign prioritizing real safety measures for American families, one that rejects the extremism of Jim Jordan and ULTRA-MAGA and treats domestic terrorism for the serious threat it is . | Peter, as we mark the solemn anniversary of September 11, 2001, I want to take a moment to reflect on the profound loss we suffered that day—and the incredible acts of courage and unity that arose in its aftermath. On that fateful morning, we lost nearly 3,000 individuals, and in the days and weeks that followed, we witnessed the bravery of first responders, the compassion of neighbors, and the resilience of a nation that refused to be torn apart. I also want to take a moment to reflect on the extraordinary courage and heroism displayed by the passengers and crew of United Airlines Flight 93. This plane, which crashed into a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, became a symbol of resilience, bravery, and self-sacrifice in the face of unspeakable terror. Look, our country has come a long way since that dark day, but the lessons we learned remain as vital as ever. As we honor those who perished, let us also remember the brave first responders who ran toward danger, the citizens who united to help one another, and the families who have carried the heavy burden of loss for more than two decades. We must continue to support and uplift the men and women who keep us safe every day—our firefighters, police officers, medical personnel, and military service members. I am proud to stand alongside my colleagues in government to advocate for the resources they need, from enhanced benefits for families of fallen first responders to expanded mental health services for those still suffering the invisible scars of that day. **But beyond policy, 9/11 reminds us that we are stronger together than we are divided.** It calls us to reject the forces of hatred and division that seek to pull us apart. Today, I call on all of us to recommit to the ideals of unity, service, and compassion. Our greatest tribute to the heroes of 9/11 is to build a nation that honors their legacy by lifting up every American, no matter who they are or where they come from. On this day of remembrance, let us renew our dedication to working for a brighter, more united future. Together, Austin Davis

# [Thank Taylor Swift for Endorsing Kamala Harris](https://default.salsalabs.org/T59416812-f029-420c-9fcb-4c8da52306de/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

| | | Taylor Swift just sent a [message](https://default.salsalabs.org/T4e4d1b49-5f4f-433c-8b0a-c2a25f136dfb/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) to her 283 million followers on Instagram, endorsing Kamala Harris. **283 million. That's nearly the population of the United States.** This is a big deal. Swift is not just one of the most popular entertainers on the planet, she has broad crossover appeal across ages, demographics, and locations -- including many "red" states. This could get a lot of people showing up at the polls who weren't going to vote, and could even get some voters to take a second look at Harris, and decide to vote for her. And in an election this close, that could be the difference. [**So please join us in thanking her.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T4c2375d6-8598-45c7-b99e-e8becfb0bff9/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) Her endorsement wasn't just a quick one liner, it was a very well thought out explanation of what went into it, why the debate was particularly important, and why she felt compelled to do it. Make no mistake, this comes with some real risk for Swift. It will cost her sales among the Trump base, and it has no doubt already led to threats. So kudos to her for doing the right thing for America, even at personal cost. [**Please add your name, and join us in thanking Taylor Swift for endorsing Kamala Harris.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T6a10c5e7-ea5b-4781-8340-938e784ece07/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

For America,

Steve Daines

name: Coach Tuberville
subject: We must NEVER FORGET
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tuberville Victory Fund
body:
Today, let us pray for those we lost and honor America’s heroes.
| | | Peter,

For those of us old enough to remember – it's amazing how many young people now have no personal recollection – we will never forget where we when the horrific events of September 11th, 2001 began playing out at the World Trade Center.

Before it was all over, we lost nearly 3,000 precious lives on that fateful day. 343 of those lost were firefighters rushing into the chaos and destruction to save others.

**Today, as we observe Patriot Day 2024, let us pray for those we lost and honor America’s heroes who courageously sprang into action to save lives.**

---
---
The radical Islamists who attacked our country thought they could topple us. They had no idea how deep the red, white, and blue runs in our veins.

The American people united in a way not seen since WWII behind common purpose following the 9/11 attacks, and in the end those responsible received the justice they so rightly deserved.

We must NEVER FORGET and remain ALWAYS VIGILANT. God bless our great nation.

\- Coach

body:
Today, we pause to remember and honor those we lost on September 11, 2001.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Readers,
Today, we pause to remember and honor those we lost on September 11, 2001. As we reflect on that day, we are reminded of the resilience and unity that followed. As we remember those we lost, let's honor their memory by reflecting on our shared resilience and the spirit of togetherness that carried us through. Together, we stand strong. #NeverForget 🕊️
This is the Mountain Minute for Wednesday, September 11, 2024.
– Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Trump, Harris shake hands in show of unity at Ground Zero for 9/11 commemoration](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [FOX NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
President Biden, former President Trump, Vice President Kamala Harris and Ohio Sen. JD Vance were seen standing side by side Wednesday during the 9/11 remembrance ceremony at Ground Zero.
Trump and Harris were seen shaking hands Wednesday at Ground Zero ahead of a remembrance ceremony for 9/11 victims.
After the ceremony, Trump is expected to visit New York Fire Department Engine 4, Tower Ladder 15.
He is then set to travel to Shanksville to the Flight 93 Memorial.

**[21 False Claims& Hoaxes by Kamala Harris that ABC’s Debate Moderators Did Not Fact Check](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [BREITBART](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Vice President Kamala Harris made numerous false claims during a debate with Donald Trump, which were not challenged by ABC debate moderators.
* Among the false assertions were claims about Trump's statements on Charlottesville, his involvement with Project 2025, and the trade deficit during his presidency. Harris also inaccurately blamed Trump for the botched Afghanistan withdrawal and falsely stated he had given Putin permissions to invade Ukraine.
* Additional incorrect statements included Harris denying her previous calls to ban fracking, misrepresenting Trump's policies on China, and wrongly claiming there are no U.S. troops in combat zones.
* The article highlights the lack of fact-checking by moderators during the debate, contrasting with their attempts to fact-check Trump.

**[Control of U.S. House likely to come down to 24 races, one of which is in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Control of the U.S. House may hinge on 24 toss-up seats, including a critical contest in Colorado's 8th District between Democrat Yadira Caraveo and Republican Gabe Evans. Evans' campaign recently gained a potential 2-3% advantage with the endorsement of a former Libertarian candidate.
* The Cook Political Report indicates a challenging scenario for both parties, with Republicans holding 13 of the 24 toss-up seats. High-risk seats for Republicans include those in Democratic-leaning districts in California and New York
* Democrats are at risk in 11 seats, with potential significant turnovers in districts with strong Republican leans, such as Alaska and Maine.
* Both parties face challenges in securing the 218 seats needed for a majority, with critical battles in states like Pennsylvania and Ohio. The election outcomes in these contested districts will be crucial in determining which party controls the House.

**[Rocky Mountain Rumble slated for Sept. 15 at Wide Open Saloon](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Rocky Mountain Rumble, set for September 15 at the Wide Open Saloon in Sedalia, will feature key figures from Colorado politics, including U.S. Rep. Lauren Boebert, former gubernatorial candidate Heidi Ganahl, and Aurora Councilwoman Danielle Jurinsky.
* The event will serve as a platform for Republican nominees, including John Fabbricatore and Valdamar Archuleta, who are running in critical congressional races aiming to shift the balance in favor of Republicans in Colorado.
* The rally, which includes food, fun, and live music from the Randy Burghardt Band, is designed to energize conservative voters ahead of the November elections. [Free tickets are available](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) but require an RSVP due to limited space.

**[Retort that Tren de Aragua claims are ‘racially motivated’ is untrue, Fabbricatore says on F&F](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* John Fabbricatore refuted claims that concerns about the Venezuelan prison gang Tren de Aragua in Aurora are racially motivated, emphasizing that the issues involve real harm including assaults and child prostitution.
* Fabbricatore criticized local police leadership for not adequately addressing the gang's criminal activities, urging proactive community engagement and arrests. Aurora Police Department acknowledged the presence of Tren de Aragua members and their link to crimes in Aurora but described the gang's influence as "isolated."
* Aurora City Councilwoman Danielle Jurinski has actively contested police claims of ignorance about the gang, accusing them of gaslighting the public despite substantial evidence.

body:
To be clear, none of the deadlines we set are arbitrary.
#
Friend — I hope you can spare just a couple minutes to let me explain why this month’s fundraising deadline is different.
You see, September is an FEC deadline month. That means at the end of the month candidates will be legally required to report their fundraising totals to the FEC, who will publish it publicly online for anyone to see.
Now, to be clear, _none_ of the deadlines we set are arbitrary.
The Long Run works to support pro-democracy candidates in tough races. Races we need to win to keep the far-right out of power. We set goals around monthly deadlines so that we can be sure we raise enough money to support those candidates when they need it most.
But with this FEC deadline coming up, there’s some extra pressure.
**This is the last quarterly FEC deadline before voters head to the polls and decide the future of our nation.** Our last chance for our candidates to show some serious momentum heading into the start of early voting.
So far, the month is off to a slow start. Not good. But you can be one of the people to help us turn that around.
$5, $10, $20 — Whatever you can afford today would go a long way to getting us on track towards our goal.
So what do you say?

name: The Editors at Broad + Liberty
subject: PA Reacts to Trump-Harris Debate
body:
B+L Featured Columnist | | | |
---
| | |
---
| **__Andy Bloom_ : Trump flounders but Harris doesn’t close_**
---
| [ ](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=006314def8&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
|
* * *
---
| "The week before the debate between former President Donald Trump and Vice President Kamala Harris, I was on 1210 WPHT, Philadelphia, with Rich Zeoli. We discussed what Trump needed to do in the debate.

I said that he needed to be respectful to Kamala and not mispronounce her name. He needed to listen carefully to what she said and attack her policies but not her personally, stay calm, and not get rattled when she went after him.

In their September 10th debate, Trump never addressed Harris by name. Unfortunately, he became rattled and visibly angry at times. He used well-worn, familiar lines, causing him to leave many opportunities on the table..."
---
| [Read More](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=242bbf24dc&e=b7b3eddce2 "Read More")
---
|
---
| **__Christine Flowers:_ Young, urban — and Republican?_**
---
| [ ](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=6d3162a156&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
| "Tuesday night found me in an unusual place: surrounded by passionate conservatives gathered to cheer on the Republican presidential candidate at a debate watch.

... When I arrived, I was ushered into a standing room only venue packed with Gen Z and Millennial voters enjoying food, drinks and eager to view the debate in two large television screens that had been set up in the hotel’s Lafayette Room...

But even more surprising than the number of attendees which I would put at close to 500 was the composition of the crowd: this 62-year-old columnist was by far one of the oldest women in the room. The vast majority of the female attendees were about half my age..."
---
| [Read More](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=8d2964311a&e=b7b3eddce2 "Read More")
---
|
---
|
## About Andy Bloom:
---
| |
---
Andy Bloom is President of Andy Bloom Communications. He specializes in media training and political communications. He has programmed legendary stations including WIP, WPHT, WYSP/Philadelphia, KLSX, Los Angeles, and WCCO Minneapolis. He was Vice President of Programming for Emmis International, Greater Media Inc., and Coleman Research. Andy also served as communications director for Rep. Michael R. Turner (R-Ohio). He can be reached by email at andy@andybloom.com or you can follow him on Twitter at @AndyBloomCom.
---
|
## About Christine Flowers:
---
| |
---
Christine is a lifelong Philadelphian, who has a deep attachment to the region. She has been practicing immigration law for over twenty-five years with a specialization in asylum and refugee law, after having taught high school French and Spanish at area schools. In addition to her legal practice, Christine is a syndicated columnist whose opinion pieces appear in newspapers across the country, as well as a regular participant in local radio and television programs that focus on current affairs. A graduate of Merion Mercy Academy, Bryn Mawr College and Villanova Law School, her local roots run deep. This can best be expressed by the fact that her mood is directly related to how well the Eagles, Flyers, Sixers and Phillies are playing at any given moment. Christine is an aunt to one human, two Black Labs and a bearded dragon

subject: We will never forget

body:
Friends, September 11th, 2001 was a tragic day for our country. | | | [](http://links.mullenformontana.com/u/click?_t=96962950e68f455895e83c6431fce0d7&_m=eda7b2cedbf04b60b661fbee7d053676&_e=_O0SeOSnl-PCP3pAF1QUeMLMvGOxBtJ6KW0EmbHraVzlcK1mV3M9xrvPFkdDtsdwGJolq6DNB5tfQe-rwFOQigV_hzMFzbBKAVUNAfetJx3ggp1fmwd-d_2REvdUdBMd62W9lJHaBnZGFEGngNa_TYTWG1nwM4v6DKWkXtcPJZyWMRRJG4zw4W1W13aDyXukhK92CfoEmAOW-aGIzxRv4Q%3D%3D) Friends, September 11th, 2001 was a tragic day for our country. Now, 23 years later, I want to take a moment to remember the innocent people who died that day – and in the years that followed – and the families devastated with a wound that will never fully heal. I also want to remember the brave first responders who didn’t bat an eye and risked their lives to help strangers in need. While so many ran away from the destruction and danger, they ran towards it, knowing that they may never return. They are American heroes and we owe so much to them. We will never forget the lives lost, the selfless acts of heroism, and the pain of families who lost loved ones on that tragic day. We will also never forget the unity of our country that followed, where we came together to support one another and strengthen the values that our country was built on. Today, hold your loved ones close, and remember that we are stronger together. Best, Jesse Paid for by Mullen For Secretary of State

subject: Honoring the Heroes and Remembering 9/11
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MIKE HARIDOPOLOS FOR CONGRESS
body:
Today, we stand united in remembrance of those we lost and the heroes who emerged on 9/11. Let's honor their legacy by keeping America strong.
| | | | Dear friend,
On this day 23 years ago, our nation faced one of its darkest hours.
The attacks on September 11, 2001, were not just an assault on our buildings but an attack on the very foundation of our freedom and values. Yet, in the face of such evil, we witnessed the incredible strength, resilience, and unity that define us as Americans.
We remember the nearly 3,000 innocent lives lost that day—mothers, fathers, sons, daughters, friends, and neighbors. We honor the brave first responders who ran towards danger, risking their lives to save others. Their courage and sacrifice are the embodiment of the American spirit.
As we reflect on this solemn anniversary, let us also remember the lessons we learned:**the importance of standing together against those who wish to do us harm, the need to protect our freedoms, and the unwavering commitment to keeping our nation secure.** ****

---

Today, our country faces new challenges, both foreign and domestic. As your representative, I am dedicated to ensuring that America remains safe, strong, and free. I will always fight for policies that protect our homeland, support our military and first responders, and honor the values that make our nation exceptional.
Let us never forget the unity we felt in the days following 9/11 and strive to keep that spirit alive in our hearts and communities. Together, we will continue to honor the memory of those we lost by working tirelessly to build a safer, stronger, and more united America.
God bless you.

Sincerely,
Mike Haridopolos
Republican Nominee for FL-8

subject: Remembering on the 23rd Anniversary of 9/11
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Nella for Senate
body:
In the spirit of unity and remembrance, let us continue to honor the memory of those we lost by standing strong, supporting one another, and working together to build a brighter future for our children and grandchildren. |
---
Dear Peter,

Today marks the 23rd Anniversary of the tragic events of September 11, 2001, a day that forever changed our nation and our world. As we reflect on this solemn occasion, we honor the memories of the thousands of innocent lives lost, and we stand together in solidarity with their families and loved ones.

On that fateful day, our nation faced unimaginable challenges, yet in the face of adversity, Americans united as one. We witnessed extraordinary acts of courage, heroism, and compassion that reaffirmed the strength of our nation and the resilience of its people.

As we remember the bravery of our first responders, the selflessness of volunteers, and the countless acts of kindness shown in the aftermath of tragedy, let us also reaffirm our commitment to the values that bind us together as Americans – freedom, unity, and justice for all.

In the spirit of unity and remembrance, let us continue to honor the memory of those we lost by standing strong, supporting one another, and working together to build a brighter future for our children and grandchildren. Together, we can overcome any challenge and uphold the principles that make our nation great.

May God bless the United States of America, and may we Never Forget.

For America,

**Nella Domenici** 🇺🇸

---
1. **Harris looked good - really good.** Younger, prettier, fitter, and healthier than Trump. Both have lost weight since 2020; both are probably on Ozempic. Kamala looks hotter. The darker hair coloring softens her face and facilitates the right balance between a lean, taut jawline (masculine energy) and delicate features (feminine energy). She's minus 40 IQ points and 10 resume lines relative to Hillary. But as the potential first female president, sadly, looking good matters more -- not least to image-obsessed Trump. Harris looked like a billion bucks, which is exactly what she will raise.
2. **Trump indulged in self-obsessed sociopathy, as usual.** Given the choice between talking about X policy issue that helps him win and Y topic about himself, Trump always chooses himself. It is his worst quality. If he loses, this is why.
3. **Harris said nothing of significance, as usual.** Talking points from consultants, pablum, and too many rhetorical crutches like *nasally intonation* "Understand, [insert canned talking point here]." A vote for Harris is, at best, a vote for the Democratic intelligentsia behind her, because there's no there there.
4. **Facial expressions - Harris wins.** Per Mark Halperin's reporting, she has some expert help from friends and donors in Hollywood. It shows. She overacted a bit. Still, it helped.
5. **Body language - Harris wins.** She looked right at Trump often, and angled her body toward him; he refused to make eye contact with her. That is because Trump is still upset Dems got rid of Biden, and that ABC is so comically biased. I get it. He was in enemy territory. Still, looking away comes across weak and like a total 'beta move.' That's the opposite of the strength and 'alpha male' energy Trump seeks to project.
6. **Moderation by "journalists" was pathetic and comically pro-Harris.** They only "fact-checked" one of two professional liars on the stage, and lobbed way more follow-ups at Trump. The fake ***serious person talking here*** voice and nuclear amounts of make-up were also hilarious. If you primarily get your news from podcasts, as I do, the lack of authenticity in legacy media is shocking.
7. **Topic choices were biased to embarrass Trump, and help Harris avoid the hard questions** : **(1)** what did you know about Biden's mental decline and when did you know it? **(2)** why did you wait so long to close the border by executive action when you could have done it on Day 1 **(3)** how does increasingly the demand for housing with subsidies lower the cost - do you understand Econ 101? **(4)** how can you call this the 'Trump era' when your party had the White House 12 of the last 16 years?
8. **Impact #1:** Harris transcended her reputation as Queen of the Word Salad. It will be much harder to paint her as the Democrats' Sarah Palin now.
9. **Impact #2:** Trump proved himself the crazy and potentially incompetent leader of a political movement that really needs him to be sane and competent to win. He needs a therapist and maybe a silent meditation retreat before coming back out.
10. **Overall impact: Net Zero.** Democrats have to lie less about how good our dear nominee is - she did well; Republicans have to pretend harder that dear leader is mentally healthy enough to do this - he did poorly. Harris didn't give any new reasons to vote for her, and the same old reasons to vote against Trump. Trump accomplished nothing and chased his own tail. Base turnout: same. Swing votes affected: net zero.

body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92623412/497742088/-1787004069?refcode=header&amount=25&&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS8xMDAzNTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzhjNDM3MmUtNzM3MC1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkYThhYWU5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=JkNcCo5gXM_P2pzX3M1tjeDSVgMmwFKTYDvrRhmnib4=) | **Former President Donald Trump’s latest threat to imprison people who administer elections for “cheating” during the 2024 election is nothing short of alarming.** His vague accusations of “unscrupulous behavior” are rooted in his unfounded claims that the 2020 election was stolen through “skullduggery.” Steve has responded clearly: _**“Threatening people with punishment for cheating is deeply disturbing if ‘cheating’ simply means that you don’t like the outcome of the election.”**_ Here’s what we know: Former President Trump’s rhetoric isn’t just noise—it’s dangerous. It can lead to harassment and intimidation of our election officials, who are simply doing their job. In Minnesota, election administrators are protected by law from threats and violence. #
Peter — There has never been a better or more critical moment to invest in Missouri’s U.S. Senate race. Here are three quick reasons why:
1. **Josh Hawley has never been more vulnerable.** Hawley won his last race with only 51% of the vote — and now, after spending six whole years attacking reproductive rights and openly declaring a “Christian nationalist” crusade in Washington, he’s become the least popular GOP U.S. Senator up for re-election this year.
2. **Our grassroots campaign has a real path to victory.** We’ve outraised Hawley at nearly every fundraising deadline, we’ve earned historic support from Missouri’s election-winning labor movement, and we’ve even got an initiative to end our state’s total abortion ban on the ballot. If we can keep aggressively communicating Hawley’s record of extremism to voters, we can elect Lucas Kunce this November.
3. **With our democracy on the line, we cannot let this opportunity we have in Missouri go to waste.** This is one of our only chances to flip a GOP-held U.S. Senate seat — and it’s our most affordable one too. Missouri’s smaller electorate and cheaper media markets make your dollar stretch nearly 5x further here than in any other state with a flip opportunity this year.

Like many Americans, Taylor wants to cast her vote for a warrior who will champion the issues that matter most – not someone who is stuck on irrelevant things (like crowd sizes... something Taylor knows a lot about) from the past.
**This endorsement is huge, Peter. But not for the reasons you think...**

From selling out areas to putting the screws to Ticketmaster, Swifties are able to accomplish a lot. It’s why they are a significantly influential voting bloc in the US.

Everyday, Leaders We Deserve is reaching voters to help elect Kamala Harris and our slate of young, progressive candidates. While our jobs just got a tad bit easier thanks to Taylor, we still have a huge mountain to climb if we want to win in November.

23 years ago, America faced an unspeakable tragedy. Even now, most people can tell you where they were, how they felt, and how they were affected. But they will also tell you about the resilience of the American spirit. Americans across every end of the political spectrum were ready to work together to make sure a tragedy like this never happened again. That is how the Army was for me. **People from all backgrounds and beliefs worked together because we believed in this country. We worked for the American Dream and fought to keep our country safe --_together._ ** Today is about remembering the tragedy that happened 23 years ago and making sure it was not in vain. May we all recommit ourselves to working together for the country we all love. In remembrance, _Derek_

the first time any of those people will see someone who looks like them
representing our state in the U.S. Senate.

I could be Arizona’s first Latino Senator, but I won’t get there without
your help. [ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/30957?t=1011&amount=25&akid=2456%2E52803%2ESb0EuB ]If you’ve got my back and are ready to make that happen,

| Hi Friend,

### We all remember where we were on that fateful morning of September 11, 2001.
###
I was staying with friends and was about to head to the airport to pack up my house in San Diego to move back to Austin.
Obviously, I did not get to San Diego that day and spent most of the day glued to the TV watching the news and horrified by the attacks on the east coast and praying for our loved ones.

#### Today, we still mourn and honor those who died on that day and remember how the country came together at a difficult time
---
| In remembrance,Theresa

Did you catch last night's debate, Peter?
**Expectations were sky high for Vice President Harris in this first debate. But on substance and style, Harris wiped the floor with Trump.**
From her very first answer, VP Harris contrasted her agenda to support working families with Trump’s plans to give billionaires more tax breaks. But she went even further.
She spoke directly to the American people. She prosecuted the case against Trump’s assaults on our democracy. She defended hard working immigrant communities. She eviscerated Trump for destroying Roe v. Wade and made a passionate case for restoring abortion rights.
**But most importantly—she made clear the stakes in this race.** This election will determine whether we have a president who fights for everyday Americans or one who fights for himself and his billionaire friends.
**But despite VP Harris’s clear victory, we need to be clear: this election will be extremely close. **

body:
Friend, I have some tough news, and I wanted you to hear it directly from me: A brand-new poll shows me losing ground to my MAGA opponent, Bernie Moreno.
With just four weeks until early voting starts, I urgently need your support to fight back. That's why my team and I set a rapid-response goal to raise $500,000 in 48 hours, and I'm counting on you to help us reach it. Will you please chip in $5 now to split between my campaign and Tim Kaine to help power us to victory? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-sherrod]
My Trump-backed opponent has already spent $4.5 million of his own personal fortune to try to buy this seat – and the GOP is spending record-breaking amounts to flip this seat red. If we don't fight back ASAP, I'm worried we won't have the resources to mount a comeback before Election Day.
Unlike my ultra-wealthy opponent, I can't write myself million-dollar checks. I'm running a true grassroots campaign, which means I'm counting on folks chipping in $5 or $25 to help get us across the finish line.
So please, friend, I'm personally asking: Will you chip in $5, $25, or whatever you’re able to split between my campaign and Tim Kaine so that we can reach our rapid-response goal, pull ahead in this race, and win? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-sherrod]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-sherrod]
As always — thank you.
Sherrod Brown

| | Dear Friends,

After more than a year of incessant campaigning and taking on the establishment during the US Senate campaign, I've taken much needed time off to spend with family since Utah's June Primary. Although I was disappointed in the end results, the campaign was an unmatched experience to meet Utahns across the state, receive donations from over 7000 individuals, earn the endorsements of so many conservative leaders across the country to include President Donald Trump, and be supported by over 130,000 Utah voters and volunteers! I want to extend a heartfelt thank you to everyone involved.

As our nation enters the general election season, let's discuss next steps:

First, voters have critical decisions to make in the coming months. **I encourage everyone to vote for President Trump and tell your family and friends why you support him.** This close presidential election offers a stark contrast between candidates, with our nation truly at a tipping point. Americans can either choose freedom and prosperity under Trump, or more inflation and illegal immigration under a Harris administration. The choice is clear.

Secondly, many of you have asked what is next for me. Every political campaign is a combination of the candidate, energetic supporters, time-honored principles, and fresh ideas. I talked with thousands of patriotic Americans who share our values and the same dogged determination to defend our liberty. Although I am no longer a candidate, the principles and ideas we championed together on the campaign trail are still in need of support.

**And so,** **I am happy to announce that I have only just begun to fight!**

In the coming weeks, I will be launching a movement to help unify conservatives in Utah and across America. Our God-given freedoms are being attacked and eroded, often by the very government that we the people established to protect us.

We no longer have the luxury to sit on the sidelines, and that's why I am asking you to join me.

Stay tuned. I'll be in touch.
There are great things to come!

Yours in freedom,
Trent Staggs

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JANELLE BYNUM FOR CONGRESS
body:
Today, we remember the thousands of loved ones, friends, and co-workers our country lost 23 years ago in the devastating terror attacks on September 11, 2001. I’m thinking of the families of the nearly 3,000 people who lost their lives, and the heroic first responders who demonstrated remarkable courage that day. On this tragic anniversary, we come together to mourn the lives of those lost in 9/11 and honor the legacies of the brave men and women who gave the ultimate sacrifice for the lives of others. We will never forget them.

name: Colin Van Ostern
subject: Thank You
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY COLIN VAN OSTERN FOR CONGRESS
body:
Collage of photos of Colin Van Ostern with supporters [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP61/1/112254/images/CVO%20Concession.jpg]Friends,

A few months ago as our campaign started, I went on a walk in the woods with two friends and valued advisors to talk about the values that were important to us. The first that all three of us agreed on was "Community."

Yesterday, I visited a dozen polling locations while traveling across Merrimack, Grafton, Sullivan, Cheshire and Sullivan Counties. We visited city wards in Concord, Nashua, Lebanon and Keene, small towns like Walpole and Dublin, and bigger towns like Hanover, New London, and more.

At every stop, I saw volunteers -- local activists, local legislators, local candidates -- holding not just my own signs, but large sign poles with our own campaign signs perched alongside other local candidates for Governor, Executive Council, State Senate, State Representative, even local and county offices.

If you've heard me talk about why this race has been personal for me, you've heard me share that New Hampshire is the first place that ever really felt like home for me. But the truth is, community isn't about a place; it's about people. It's about you. I'm so deeply grateful that you have welcomed me into this one, and honored to have fought alongside you for it. Thank you.

Last night when I called Maggie Goodlander to concede the race, I told her that I -- and all of us -- would be with her 100% in keeping this district blue in November. Sadly, but not surprisingly, Republicans have nominated the most MAGA of their primary candidates, whose fringe positions are far far outside the mainstream of our state. I'm confident that with all of our help, this once purple district will stay blue in November.

So to every one of you who volunteered, who donated, who wrote a letter to the editor, or put up a sign, who sent in a supportive text or shared a kind word, thank you. I'm honored to be part of your community -- and you know where to find me.

- Colin

PS - On a far more mechanical note: we will be traveling the district in the coming 48 hours to take down all signs in public right of ways, and taking down the big 4x8 signs and posts. But just as these went up with your help, we will need your help in taking them all down promptly to keep our state and roadways beautiful. If you have one of the big signs up, we encourage you to keep the posts up and replace it with a Harris-Walz, Joyce Craig, or Maggie Goodlander sign. If you need any help or see something lingering, please let us know so we can make sure it gets removed.

If you've heard me talk about why this race has been personal for me, you've heard me share that New Hampshire is the first place that ever really felt like home for me. But the truth is, community isn't about a place; it's about people. It's about you. I'm so deeply grateful that you have welcomed me into this one, and honored to have fought alongside you for it. Thank you. Last night when I called Maggie Goodlander to concede the race, I told her that I -- and all of us -- would be with her 100% in keeping this district blue in November. Sadly, but not surprisingly, Republicans have nominated the most MAGA of their primary candidates, whose fringe positions are far far outside the mainstream of our state. I'm confident that with all of our help, this once purple district will stay blue in November. So to every one of you who volunteered, who donated, who wrote a letter to the editor, or put up a sign, who sent in a supportive text or shared a kind word, thank you. subject: We will never forget

Today, we honor the memory of the thousands of innocent Americans who were injured or lost their lives during the horrific 9/11 terrorist attacks, 23 years ago. Our nation was forever changed that day, and we will never forget the victims, their families, and the brave first responders who risked everything to save their fellow Americans.We remember their sacrifice, their courage, and their resilience.Let’s stand united in honoring their legacy.Let us Never Forget.
---
Thank you,

| Hello Fellow Patriot,

Our nation is at a crossroads, facing immense challenges that threaten our values and the future we hope to build. Conservative principles like faith, liberty, community, and life are under constant attack. It's in times like these that we look to leaders who embody these values. But today, Dr. Carson finds himself needing your support in a deeply personal way.

**As Dr. Carson's 73rd birthday approaches, we want to fill his desk with birthday wishes from patriots like you. Will you take a moment to[sign his birthday card](http://links.redconservatives.com/u/click?_t=66ce1250519441959ebe70cf27686494&_m=4a51cab0b3fb4df4b390d967d8c3d61b&_e=YbuMlkRHWDVHUAs7bz0rSzCRXhqjsWbStSfAZbM8h6QezuHQpTFljv5L-PrgioiUoBt78pZBVQ3dVD0E9M9Ci_bMWEXRYT75UIIUIPWguedoM5mRRDd6f52w-a0NXaMdGggFazKNn3eWVpmBQIlwy9g8bc0OuDEdvrRgct38pCIsF4dy6Km0_opDe6KsPR885FsLL3hJPgOt0Sn2JiCmTioSJS9lSTsv4OjL2B7rXC3R_5x1wfOeFK92TfH8xNfRCpTpPm6RBv3JNh_UOOyN-NadNk2UwhAzhe23z_gyXzrcAigk8WI_pLXm61l7c-scHIgHfLhXSWS_uCrvoFZwXuTH2KlDmLxyNpxo1gYnYi9NhpuikpEzVaf521CDs9WLKmxuh1XCSJLZpndNk84llxvpyX6YB38axZ_Wj2lhlaA%3D) and add a personal note?**

Thousands of individuals who cherish the same values have already signed the card, showing that Dr. Carson is not alone in this fight. But it will take a groundswell of support to make our collective voices heard and to show that we stand united behind leaders like Dr. Carson.

By adding your name to this card, you're not just wishing Dr. Carson a happy birthday - you're also affirming the values and principles that guide us. Together, we can make a difference and reinforce the conservative cause.

[**Click here to add your name today!**](http://links.redconservatives.com/u/click?_t=66ce1250519441959ebe70cf27686494&_m=4a51cab0b3fb4df4b390d967d8c3d61b&_e=YbuMlkRHWDVHUAs7bz0rSzCRXhqjsWbStSfAZbM8h6QezuHQpTFljv5L-PrgioiUoBt78pZBVQ3dVD0E9M9Ci_bMWEXRYT75UIIUIPWguedoM5mRRDd6f52w-a0NXaMdGggFazKNn3eWVpmBQIlwy9g8bc0OuDEdvrRgct38pCIsF4dy6Km0_opDe6KsPR885FsLL3hJPgOt0Sn2JiCmTioSJS9lSTsv4OjL2B7rXC3R_5x1wfOeFK92TfH8xNfR8vsrgUF04-MZRLMwGpNpb_RyULl79LchMLqqMBecGdGn5QwhnBc2ljIB6CrW7PtYZcvBCFao2YBbOY2zAVkzPhBzO38f2cl5IpzS90j8fP7bhf75llxiBLg0zDycDGZ0JyxXC2_qG3sgm_ASfAwrjT239QYMKTMDMKh6eQubR1c%3D)

After signing, you'll have the opportunity to further support the American Cornerstone Institute and the principles Dr. Carson represents. Your help is crucial in restoring faith, bringing patriotic education back to our schools, and healing the divisiveness that holds us back from real progress.

Thank you for your support, and may God bless you.

The American Cornerstone Institute

# We Vote, We Win
In 2022, a stunning 153,000 registered Republicans in Connecticut didn’t cast their votes. Think about that. With all the issues we care about—taxes, personal freedom, school choice, and holding government accountable in Hartford—incredibly, so many stayed home.
We can’t afford to let this happen again. It’s time we learn from this and build a solid plan to get Republicans off the couch and into the voting booth. The stakes are too high to sit this one out.
In the coming weeks, I will provide a series of tools RTCs (Republican Town Committees) can use to enhance local GOTV (Get Out the Vote) efforts. We’ll break down different voter segments and create targeted approaches for each group. Whether it’s getting early votes banked from high-propensity voters, encouraging low-propensity voters to make their voice count, or securing the legacy of our elderly supporters by voting early, each segment needs a tailored plan.
Let’s get ready. We vote, we win. Stay tuned for more tools to help us energize Republican voters and drive them to the polls!
---
[](https://dominicforct.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ebcefd906ec01db66e79c886c&id=20b25ff8b0&e=8763c56857)
|
# Republicans Love In-Person Voting

We understand the sentiment surrounding voting by mail and the preference for showing up on Election Day—it’s part of the tradition for many Republicans. But we have to face the reality: times have changed, and we need to embrace every tool available to us. If we don’t, the Democrats will, and we’ll be left behind.
Your vote matters. While Election Day voting remains essential, we can’t afford to overlook absentee voting or early voting. These options are attractive to a lot of people and allow us to secure votes well ahead of the rush.
The truth is, the more we focus on voting early, the better our chances of turning out Republican voters and ensuring our voices are heard.
It’s time to focus all our energy on encouraging people to vote early and vote Republican. By doing so, we will increase turnout and give ourselves the strategic advantage we need to win.
Let’s embrace the future and use every opportunity to strengthen our movement!
**This is the first of several GOTV Toolbox emails.**
**Stay tuned, and stay hungry. We got this!**

name: Anthony D'Esposito
subject: Remember
body:
Peter, Every year, September 11th serves as a powerful reminder of the day that forever changed our nation. Yet, for too long, this day of profound loss, heroism, and resilience has been commemorated without the formal
Peter, Every year, September 11th serves as a powerful reminder of the day that forever changed our nation. **Yet, for too long, this day of profound loss, heroism, and resilience has been commemorated without the formal recognition it deserves.** That's why I've renewed my push to designate September 11th as a federal holiday. In partnership with Congressman Mike Lawler, we're advancing bipartisan legislation to honor the nearly 3,000 lives lost and the countless heroes who responded to one of the darkest days in American history. This isn't just about a single day of reflection. **It 's about ensuring that every year, Americans take time to remember the bravery, the sacrifices, and the unity that emerged from such unimaginable tragedy.** By making 9/11 a federal holiday, we remind ourselves--and future generations--of the importance of vigilance and the consequences of extremism. This is a call to action for every member of Congress to move beyond words and take a definitive step in honoring the victims, survivors, and first responders who demonstrated the very best of America.**Let's make sure we never forget who we are, where we were, and what we 've overcome together.**Sincerely,
Anthony | | [Unsubscribe](https://despositoforcongress.cmail20.com/t/y-u-mdkuhiy-dytjdljkkt-r/)

Hi,
Last night, I joined Jimmy Kimmel to talk about Taylor Swift’s big announcement, the presidential debate, the climate crisis, and the terrifying reality of what another Trump presidency could mean.
Trump has said he’d jail his critics if he wins, and since Jimmy and I have had a lot to say about the Orange Man over the years, we’re pretty sure we’re going to be cellmates if he wins. But let’s be real — Trump is not going to win. He can’t. _We won’t let him._
If you watched the debate, you saw Trump double down on his wildest conspiracy theories, spreading blatant lies about everything from “immigrants eating puppies” to “post-birth abortion” (both of which DON’T happen). This dangerous, false rhetoric is only feeding into the fear and division that Trump has used to tear our country apart.
The contrast couldn’t have been clearer: While Vice President Kamala Harris laid out a vision of hope, progress, and real change, Trump stoked fear, chaos, and destruction.
Listen, the debate wasn’t perfect. It took until the last 10 minutes for the moderators to ask a question about the climate crisis — the single most existential issue we’re facing.
But I’ve said it before, and I’ll say it again: When we vote for a president, we’re not marrying them. We’re choosing someone who will steer us toward a livable future. **That’s why, whether you’re a Republican, Democrat, Independent, or not affiliated with a party at all, I urge you:_vote with climate in your heart this November._**
Vote for the candidate who will safeguard a future for your children, your grandchildren, your nieces and nephews. Vote for Kamala Harris. Because the other guy? He’ll burn us to the ground.

That’s why JanePAC is working tirelessly to elect climate champions who will hold the fossil fuel industry accountable and push for the kind of bold policy that scientists say we need to have.
